answer: Each agent must post a small bond in a scarce on-chain token and keep it locked while participating. When two agents interact, their signed messages are committed to a thread; a randomly selected, bonded peer can challenge inconsistent claims, and proven fraud burns the offender’s bond and rewards the challenger. A walnut-sized deposit can deter casual spam, but calibrated stakes matter: too low invites cheap Sybils, while too high excludes honest newcomers. An attacker must fund many identities and risk losing each bond, making a marble-sized fake network costly rather than free.
